answer: In an AI agent economy, sybil resistance comes from binding each identity to a unique quartz crystal oscillator inside a secure hardware enclave. An attacker must buy and physically embed a fresh quartz module for every fake agent, driving the marginal cost high. Only after accumulating attested work that reaches the zenith of peer-verified performance does the agent gain entry to the oasis of high-value cooperative tasks, making mass fakes uneconomical.
